transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Marina Lopez (Redwood SE), Tariq Bose (Redwood Partnerships), Alex Duarte (MeridianOps VP Partnerships), Priya Nair (MeridianOps CTO), Samir Khan (MeridianOps Platform Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
MeridianOps is a regional reseller and systems integrator focusing on mid-market SaaS companies in EMEA and APAC. They want to explore a partnership to resell Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private offering as part of their managed GPU stack, plus an integration pattern for quick onramp for customers that need a VPC-connected private inference path. Main concerns: data residency, auditability (SOC2/ISO), pricing margining, and validation of Redwood runtime on MeridianOps' selected GPU SKUs. Redwood team (AE+SE) to provide integration brief, test account, and schedule technical deep dive for performance benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- MeridianOps business model and go-to-market (resale + managed deployment)
- Technical constraints: preferred GPU SKUs (A200 / H100 equivalents), on-prem connectivity, VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration
- Compliance and audit: SOC2 type 2, ISO27001, customer audit support, log retention
- Commercial mechanics: margining, committed capacity, lead times for dedicated pools
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Action items (auto section):
See metadata.action_items above.

Full transcript (note: occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker attribution errors expected):
[00:00] Jordan Li: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we tried to keep this to 45-ish minutes but happy to go longer. Jordan from Redwood… AE for partnerships.
[00:14] Alex Duarte: Hi Jordan, Alex here. Thanks for setting this up, we've got Priya and Samir on from the technical side, and I'm curious to hear how Redwood thinks about a reseller+managed offering.
[00:25] Marina Lopez: Hi all, Marina, solutions engineering. We'll mostly start high-level then Marina can hand to me — sorry, hand to Jordan for the commercials then dive deep with Marina — small brain fart —
[00:37] Priya Nair: No worries. Priya CTO. Quick note, we are evaluating partners who can operate in EU and APAC with strong compliance, and low-latency routing between customer VPCs and vendor infra.
[00:50] Samir Khan: Samir, platform. We'll be the team operating the on-prem and hybrid clusters if we move forward. We're focused on throughput for batch embedding workloads and tail latency for chat use-cases.
[01:05] Jordan Li: Great. Quick agenda: 1) understand MeridianOps GTM/targets, 2) technical fit and constraints (hardware SKUs, VPC peering, KMS), 3) pilot scoping and next steps. Does that sound okay?
[01:15] Alex Duarte: Yep sounds good.
[01:20] Jordan Li: Cool. Quick question Alex — typical size of customer you're targeting for this offering? Mid-market SaaS with 500 to 5k employees?
[01:28] Alex Duarte: Exactly, mostly B2B SaaS, some AI-first startups but mostly enterprise-looking buyers that want quick integration and a managed GPU offering. We handle infra, so we want a partner model where we can resell Redwood Dedicated and also offer Redwood Private for customers with strict data residency.
[01:45] Marina Lopez: Two quick clarifications — Redwood Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool in our cloud with SLAs; Redwood Private is a private control plane (VPC or on-prem) where customers' data stays in their network. Both can be routed from your managed environment with routing policies.
[02:02] Priya Nair: Important for us: can Redwood integrate with an HSM for key management? We need KMS/HSM integrations for certain banking customers.
[02:12] Marina Lopez: Yes, we support KMS integrations; for Private on-prem we also have options to integrate with customer-managed HSMs via standard APIs. There are some configuration steps and an enterprise support engagement typically.
[02:27] Samir Khan: What about audit logs? Our customers often want 12-24 month retention and per-token cost breakdowns.
[02:36] Jordan Li: We provide per-route and token-level telemetry via the Console, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3 with configurable retention. For Private deployments you control that retention window.
[02:50] Alex Duarte: Sounds promising. On the hardware side, what's the supported GPU list? We mainly run A200-equivalent and H100 class in our managed clusters.
[02:59] Marina Lopez: Our runtime supports modern transformer models optimized across shapes, and we validate on a matrix of GPU SKUs — A100/A200 equivalents, H100 and NVLink variants. For the reseller model we can publish supported kernel profiles per SKU. For Private we'll help with a compatibility runbook.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Is there an easy migration path between Dedicated and Private? Say a customer starts on Dedicated and later wants to shift to Private with same model pins and rollout policies.
[03:30] Jordan Li: Yeah that's one of our differentiators — same API surface and rollout primitives across deployment modes. You can pin model versions and we can help export and import model artifacts and config. There are operational steps (KV cache warmup, potential quantized model differences) that SE will help with.
[03:48] Samir Khan: Quantization — do you provide quantized model artifacts or do customers do quantization in-house?
[03:55] Marina Lopez: We have recommended quantization profiles and can provide quantized variants for a set of curated models. For custom models, we provide tooling and guidance. There can be trade-offs we can show in latency/cost reports.
[04:09] Alex Duarte: Commercially, we need to understand margining. We resell and operate — how flexible are committed capacity or wholesale pricing?
[04:18] Jordan Li: We have partner pricing tiers for resellers, with committed capacity discounts. There's flexibility in contractual terms depending on volume and regions. We'll follow up with a partner pricing matrix.
[04:29] Alex Duarte: Great. A few technical deep-dive points from Priya: 1) network topology — can we do VPC peering or do you prefer a private link? 2) control plane isolation for Private offering? 3) observability hooks — traces and token-level attribution.
[04:46] Priya Nair: On the VPC side, some customers cannot allow inbound peering and prefer egress-only via private link endpoints. That matters because of firewall rules and SOC.
[04:55] Marina Lopez: For Hosted/Dedicated we offer private link and peering depending on cloud. For Private, customers control their control plane; for VPC-connected Private deployments we can set up outbound-only peering with mutually agreed CIDR ranges. We'll need to map exact network flows during the pilot.
[05:16] Samir Khan: For the pilot, we'll want to run two workloads: 1) dense embedding batch (throughput-focused) and 2) chat low-latency tail (p99 emphasis). Can you run both on a small pool so we can see trade-offs?
[05:29] Marina Lopez: Absolutely. SE can provision a small test cluster (we typically recommend 1-2 A200s and 1 H100 for comparative runs) and we can run the benchmarks with your sample prompts.
[05:42] Alex Duarte: Who will own the benchmarking infra? MeridianOps or Redwood? We prefer Redwood runs the initial benchmarks to validate performance and then we'll run in our environment.
[05:51] Jordan Li: Redwood will run the initial validation and provide results and scripts. Then we can hand off the configs so you can run the same tests on your SKUs.
[06:03] Priya Nair: Security — does Redwood support SAML SSO/SCIM for partner-managed accounts? We want RBAC tied to our identity fabric.
[06:11] Marina Lopez: Yes, SAML and SCIM are supported for user provisioning and RBAC. For Private, you can integrate with your IdP and enforce your policies.
[06:20] Alex Duarte: Pricing cadence — monthly billed for Dedicated? Committed annual? Need to understand how we invoice customers.
[06:29] Jordan Li: Hosted/Dedicated is usage + reserved capacity model (monthly billing for usage and monthly for reserved). For reseller deals we can enable invoicing flows that suit your operation, and we do white-label or reseller SKUs in specific agreements. Tariq on partnerships will follow up on the commercial template.
[06:47] Tariq Bose: Yep I'll coordinate the commercial template and partner program documentation.
[06:52] Samir Khan: A small nit — we usually have to satisfy bank customers with explicit subnet-level routing and KMS key policies. Is there a reference architecture?
[07:03] Marina Lopez: We have a partner integration guide and reference topology diagrams, I'll attach them. There's also a security compliance pack with SOC2 and architecture notes.
[07:15] Alex Duarte: Good. On timelines: if we want a pilot in December, what's realistic?
[07:22] Jordan Li: If we start the paperwork this week, SE can provision a test cluster and we could run initial bench by the second week of December. Pilot could start mid-December depending on procurement cycles.
[07:34] Priya Nair: Procurement is avg two to three weeks for smaller customers; for enterprise might be longer. We'll surface a pilot customer that has faster procurement.
[07:44] Marina Lopez: A few follow-up technical clarifications for the benchmark run: we need sample prompt sets for chat, corpus for embeddings, target sequence lengths, target batch sizes, and expected latency SLOs.
[07:58] Samir Khan: We'll provide the sample data — likely 512 token average for chat and 1k-2k token windows for embeddings jobs. For throughput we expect to saturate with batch sizes of 128-512 for embeddings.
[08:13] Jordan Li: Great. We'll send a benchmark template.
[08:18] Alex Duarte: Quick question about model provenance — some of our customers care about model lineage and fine-tuning. Does Redwood track model versions and provide rollout control for fine-tuned variants?
[08:27] Marina Lopez: Yes, model cataloging, version pins and rollouts are supported. We also support function calling and structured outputs. We keep model metadata in the control plane and can provide audit trails for model changes.
[08:42] Priya Nair: For Private, does the control plane ever talk to Redwood-hosted services for updates or is it fully isolated? Some of our customers disallow any outbound control plane traffic.
[08:55] Jordan Li: For fully air-gapped Private deployments we have an on-prem package and update tooling that doesn't require outbound telemetry. For VPC-connected Private, there may be optional outbound to pull updates; we can disable if required but updates then become manual. We'll surface the on-prem package details.
[09:15] Speaker 1: [indistinct] — quick, uh clarification about latency numbers and kernel selection that Marina mentioned earlier, could you spell that out again?
[09:26] Marina Lopez: Sure, so our compilation and kernel selection chooses optimized kernels based on model shape and sequence length distribution. That means we can reduce p99 by picking lower-latency kernels for shorter sequences, and choose larger batch-optimized kernels for throughput jobs. It's part of the runtime compaction.
[09:47] Samir Khan: Any constraints on model size? We have customers using 7B to 70B variants.
[09:54] Marina Lopez: We support a wide range but larger models have memory and latency trade-offs; for 70B we typically recommend H100 class or multi-GPU shards with NVLink. We'll include recommended SKUs per model size in the runbook.
[10:08] Jordan Li: Let's talk pilot success criteria — Alex, what are you looking for?
[10:15] Alex Duarte: 1) Verified performance on MeridianOps hardware (throughput/latency) 2) Clear partner commercial terms and margin 3) Security/compliance checklist validated 4) Simple onboarding flow for our operations team.
[10:29] Jordan Li: Perfect. We'll align on KPIs and make sure SE produces a short report.
[10:35] Priya Nair: On the compliance side we need evidence for SOC2 + assistance for customer audits (attestation). Do you provide audit support?
[10:44] Marina Lopez: Yes we provide SOC2 reports and can support customer audits; for Private we also provide documentation for on-prem deployments. We have an enterprise pack for audit readiness.
[10:56] Samir Khan: Networking deep-dive — can we get sample iptables/firewall rules and CIDR requirements early? That will speed up network approvals.
[11:05] Jordan Li: We'll include a network appendix in the integration brief with ports, CIDRs, and best-practice firewall rules.
[11:13] Alex Duarte: A couple of competitive angles — some customers ask why choose Redwood over Lambda or an AWS native endpoint. What's the short pitch for us so we can position it to customers?
[11:23] Tariq Bose: Quick pitch: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with strong latency/cost controls, partner-friendly commercial flows, and production-first tooling like token-level breakdowns and rollout controls. We also publish performance profiles per model/SKU.
[11:39] Jordan Li: Also emphasize our onboarding velocity and support for private deployments with KMS and audit logs — that resonates with regulated verticals.
[11:48] Alex Duarte: Good. Anything else on the tech side?
[11:52] Samir Khan: One more — what's the process for adding a new GPU SKU to the compatibility matrix? We onboard custom hardware sometimes.
[12:01] Marina Lopez: We have a hardware onboarding process — initial compatibility run, kernel tuning, and then model validation. Timeline varies but for common SKUs it's usually 2-4 weeks.
[12:12] Priya Nair: Sounds reasonable.
[12:16] Jordan Li: Ok, wrap-up and recaps — we'll send the partner brief, network appendix, pricing matrix, and benchmark template. SE will provision a temporary test account. MeridianOps to send pilot customer list and any hard compliance constraints. We'll aim to schedule the performance deep dive week of 11/22.
[12:36] Alex Duarte: That works. We'll circulate internal stakeholders and pick a pilot.
[12:40] Jordan Li: Thanks all. We'll follow-up via email with the docs and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[12:47] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone.
[12:50] Marina Lopez: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
